PullRequest.Title: chat: serialize agent customization resolution
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

Related to #340978.

Customization refresh events could launch overlapping scans and discard completed results, delaying custom agents in the picker until a scan survived the startup event burst.

Use `ThrottledDelayer` to serialize scans per scope and coalesce pending refreshes. Publish completed results immediately, then refresh with current inputs. Preserve provider-specific scopes and prevent publication after disposal.

Regression tests cover first-result publication during an event burst, one coalesced follow-up scan, and disposal with work in flight.

### Validation

- `node build\next\index.ts transpile` — passed.
- `node test\unit\browser\index.js --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\agentSessions\agentHostClientTools.test.ts --browser chromium --grep 'AgentHostClientTools' --reporter dot` — 90 passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Client type-checking did not complete: the compiler exhausted memory, including a retry with an 8 GB heap.
- Targeted oxlint did not run successfully because dependency restoration was incomplete.
- Live Remote-SSH startup timing was not remeasured.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A debounce-only scheduler admitted overlapping full customization scans whenever refresh events were separated by more than 50 ms but scans took longer. Extra scans repeated discovery, extension-provider IPC and agent reads, queued redundant bundled-content traversals, and invalidated completed initial results, delaying the custom-agent picker and session claim until a newer scan completed without being superseded.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: During a startup customization-event burst on slow discovery or remote filesystems, completed initial scans could be discarded, delaying picker population and the session-claim critical path while redundant scan I/O accumulated. This is established by scheduling and call-path evidence, not a measured timing result.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The added ThrottledDelayer construction serializes scans within each shared session-type/root-set scope and coalesces eligible pending refreshes into one follow-up. Replacing the sequence guard with a disposal guard allows the first completed scan to publish and settle initial resolution instead of waiting for a scan that survives overlapping refreshes. Existing per-authority bundle sequencing and per-bundler I/O limits remain intact; independent scopes remain independent.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The deleted base line 157 constructs a plain Delayer with a 50 ms debounce. Delayer.trigger (async.ts:443-454) clears completionPromise before invoking the asynchronous task, so another event after the debounce can start another scan before the previous one finishes. Scope listeners include prompt changes, sync-provider changes, plugin and MCP observable changes, and skill-folder file changes. Each scan enumerates prompt locations once, then runs resolveCustomizationRefs and resolveLocalCustomAgents concurrently. Local/user listings perform filesystem discovery and extension listings invoke provider IPC; custom-agent resolution reads each enabled agent file. Bundling is already sequenced per authority and limits source file operations to 10 per bundler, but each extra scan still enqueues another content-read/hash traversal. The deleted sequence guard discards completed results if a later scan has begun, and initial resolution completes only for an accepted scan. ActiveClientEntry.claim awaits scope.whenResolved (agentHostSessionHandler.ts:1304), and ambient draft agents feed the picker (agentHostChatContribution.ts:415-417). The added test at agentHostClientTools.test.ts:288-349 holds a scan open while ten changes arrive 100 ms apart and establishes one scan during the burst, first-result publication, and two total scans. Blame identifies c14ff798a753dc8afcf8081ffe90a4763a9ee226 as introducing the old Delayer construction.

Scenarios.Scenario: Initial customization discovery and custom-agent picker population in local, Agents, and Remote-SSH windows.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the existing 50 ms debounce, enumerateLocalCustomizationsForHarness must finish, followed by both reference/bundle resolution and agent metadata resolution. Only then are agents published and initial resolution settled. Ambient scopes feed AgentCustomizationItemProvider without waiting for host parsing. The PR permits the first completed scan to publish instead of discarding it when another scan has started.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover customization files through directory resolution, skill discovery, and optional parent-repository stat calls; configured glob locations use the existing search-service boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per scan, work scales with configured locations and discovered directories, plus parent depth when enabled. Explicit skill roots are listed once per normalized root when built-in override filtering applies. URI sets deduplicate resulting files, not necessarily directory visits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical discovery per scan, but debounce-only scheduling could run multiple scans concurrently during a slow startup burst.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery must finish before either downstream resolver can finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One invocation per applicable dynamic provider per scan, not per returned file; providers of a type are awaited sequentially. Static contribution promises do not repeat provider IPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same provider calls occurred in every overlapping scan. The PR coalesces scans rather than adding provider calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Enumeration awaits provider results and extension registration/activation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stat each unique eligible plugin root, read enabled agent files, traverse/read included loose-file and skill trees, and update synthetic bundles in an in-memory filesystem.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stat per unique forwarded plugin URI per scan; one metadata read per eligible agent; bundle traversal/read work per included source file and directory. Up to two aggregate synthetic bundles, not one bundle per source file. Content reads/hashes remain on warm scans; tree writes occur only for changed nonces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same operations occurred for each admitted scan. Bundle sequencing already prevented concurrent rewrites within an authority but did not coalesce repeated traversals.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both metadata reads and bundle preparation are awaited before initial publication. Remote-SSH source URIs route through RemoteFileSystemProviderClient and disk-provider channel calls; synthetic destination writes are in memory.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Unique shared session-type/root-set scopes; configured local/user discovery locations, workspace/root count, registered extension providers, unique installed plugin URIs, enabled agent files, and all included skill-directory files after filtering. Multiple consumers of an equivalent scope do not multiply scans.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One active scan and one coalesced eligible follow-up per scope, rather than overlapping debounce-triggered scans. Prompt types are enumerated sequentially, storage sources within a type concurrently, and reference/agent resolution concurrently. Agent reads use Promise.all. Each of two bundlers has a 10-operation source-I/O limiter and existing per-authority sequencing. Different scopes have no new global serialization or limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: listPromptFilesForStorage bypasses the general cachedFileLocations getter: local/user filesystem discovery and dynamic extension providers are revisited per scan. Static extension contributions share their stored promises; Agents built-in skills share a discovery promise, including empty results. Bundlers still read and hash source contents on warm scans, but matching content nonces skip virtual-tree rewrites. Scope equality checks suppress unchanged observable publications. Failures settle initial resolution and do not create an automatic retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: scheduler implementation, all scope refresh listeners, resolver call paths, caches, bundler limits, picker wiring, and changed deterministic burst test were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No live latency measurement; source-tree size, dynamic-provider duration, remote latency, and startup event frequency vary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced high-confidence regression. The diff fixes overlapping/redundant scans and delayed initial publication; introducing-commit provenance was recorded through report_regression_fix.

Scenarios.Scenario: Claiming a new session and propagating customization changes to existing sessions or provisional drafts.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ActiveClientEntry.claim awaits scope.whenResolved, then a microtask reconciliation and local dispatch before settling; normal refresh reconciliation uses an existing 5 ms delayer. Provisional bindings publish only for resolved scopes with an existing generation. Host materialization remains asynchronous after outgoing dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the composed SessionActiveClientSet action via the existing agent-host transport and grant connection-deduplicated implicit reads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One action per reconciled changed backend-session snapshot, subject to existing 5 ms coalescing and equality suppression; provisional bindings publish per observable update with a live generation. First-result publication can precede one coalesced changed follow-up.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Used the same transport, payload and reconciliation logic, but superseded scan results were discarded. Publishing completed results earlier is the intended availability tradeoff; unchanged snapshots retain suppression.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session claim waits for local reconciliation/dispatch, not completion of host-side plugin copying.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize forwarded plugin directories, check warm nonce destinations, persist cache ordering and perform existing stale-revision cleanup; source copying can cross the client-resource transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per effective plugin URI/nonce cache miss, one tree copy whose internal work scales with tree size. Warm hits check destination existence and persist cache; equal Copilot controller inputs skip the manager entirely. Different chat fan-out calls do not imply separate Copilot copies because the controller and per-URI cache are shared.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical manager operations and cache policy. The PR does not add per-file publications, alter nonces, defeat cache hits, or change host synchronization limits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host customization readiness depends on materialization and parsing, but this is off the local claim-dispatch critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One scan per shared scope, followed by publication per attached backend session/draft whose composed state changes. Payload size scales with tool definitions and unique plugin refs plus at most two bundle refs, not all bundled files. Host fan-out visits session chats; Copilot shares the owning session controller and suppresses identical client inputs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Upstream scans are serialized/coalesced per scope. Outgoing dispatch is fire-and-forget. Copilot sync chains per client; Claude queues existing-chat sync per session; AgentPluginManager sequences per plugin URI while different URIs sync concurrently. No changed global burst or new process launch is established.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Scope deep equality checks remain. ActiveClientEntry suppresses snapshots matching host state or its last publication. Provisional publication lacks that extra client-side check, as before. Copilot SessionPluginController skips equal inputs. AgentPluginManager caches materialization by URI/nonce with a destination-existence check; cold or nonce-less refs copy the tree, warm nonce hits skip copying but retain existing cache-persistence I/O. Failed results are not newly retried by this PR.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for initial-resolution gating, publication, transport, host fan-out, and materialization/cache paths. No independently harmful increase in downstream work was established beyond intentionally publishing useful completed snapshots.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host tree-copy duration and attached session/chat counts vary; no runtime timing was measured.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Earlier publication unblocks session claims; unchanged payloads, equality suppression and host cache/sequencing remain. The intentional first-result/follow-up scheduling change alone does not prove harmful fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Several providers or sessions with equivalent, differing, ambient, or empty working-directory root sets.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each distinct scope resolves independently; consumers sharing equivalent normalized roots observe the same result. Provider registration owns an ambient scope while session/provisional scopes use their working-directory sets.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register skill-folder watchers and execute the discovery/read boundaries described in the initial-discovery scenario for each distinct scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing watcher count is three default skill folders per normalized explicit root per scope. Scan work multiplies by distinct keys, not scope reference count; each key coalesces pending refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same normalized keys, reference sharing and watchers; each key could additionally admit overlapping scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watcher registration does not add a new awaited phase; each consumer waits only for its own scope's initial scan.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K distinct session-type/root-set keys, after root URI deduplication and sorting. Equivalent consumers do not add scopes. Ambient undefined roots and empty roots intentionally remain distinct; per-root watchers scale with three default skill locations per explicit root.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one active scan per scope; up to K independent scans across keys. There is no global scan limiter, but the PR reduces within-key concurrency and does not increase K, watcher count, or registration frequency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The unchanged scope map shares active scopes by provider/root-set identity and removes them after the last reference. Sync-provider instances remain stable per session type. Existing discovery/bundle caches have the same ownership and keys; scope recreation can require fresh bundling as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: scope identity normalization, map sharing, provider-specific bundler authorities, reference ownership, callers and existing scope-sharing tests were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of distinct simultaneously active scope keys is product/user dependent. No aggregate resource measurement was available.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced cross-scope concurrency or retention regression. The scheduler is deliberately per scope and preserves existing sharing and lifecycle.

Scenarios.Scenario: Disposing the last scope reference, closing a draft, or removing a provider while a scan and refresh are pending.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Disposal completes the initial-resolution promise, unregisters listeners/watchers and removes the scope immediately; it does not await outstanding I/O. Late scan results do not publish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Allow already-started discovery/agent reads to settle while preventing queued refreshes and new bundle file operations; unregister existing skill-folder watchers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: No queued refresh executes after disposal. Residual work is bounded by the active scan and already-started bundler operations; the bundler's existing source-I/O limit is 10 each. Earlier versions could have multiple residual scans.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Delayer disposal canceled only pending debounce work; sequence invalidation suppressed publication but did not cancel already-started parallel scans. Bundler draining and watcher cleanup already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cleanup and late I/O do not delay scope-release completion or initial-resolution promise settlement.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Outstanding work in one active scan per disposed scope and at most one coalesced queued follow-up. Remaining discovery/agent reads scale with the already-started scan, not future events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ThrottledDelayer.dispose cancels its timer and disposes Throttler; its completion continuation checks cancellation before starting queued work. Already-started I/O settles asynchronously. Before the PR several scans could already be in flight.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scheduler and scope are disposed; queued factories are cleared. Existing in-flight enumeration and agent reads use CancellationToken.None, while bundlers reject further operations after disposal and drain their existing file-operation limiter. No new persistent map or negative-cache state is added.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: disposal implementations, reference release, map removal and the added in-flight/queued-disposal test were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Duration of already-started provider or remote filesystem operations is unknown; their non-cancellation is pre-existing.
Scenarios.Verdict: No cleanup or retained-resource regression introduced. The change additionally prevents queued refresh execution and preserves suppression of late publication.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over the complete two-file inventory and every diff hunk. Inspected scheduling, scope ownership/callers, discovery and extension IPC, source and virtual filesystem work, publication/transport, host cache/materialization, and disposal. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance findings qualify. Recorded one concrete missing-coalescing regression fix with base-line blame provenance. Static analysis only; no runtime profiling. The requested guide document exceeded the tool's output limit; loaded skill instructions and available supporting guidance were applied.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
